newsitem.title: USA: Rockwell to ship new modem chipsets in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Rockwell to ship new modem chipsets in Feb.

text.p: Rockwell International Corp said Monday it plans to begin production shipment of its K56 modem chipsets this month.
The company said it has shipped samples of the new high speed modem chips to more than 130 customers and is on schedule to begin production in February, as planned.
Rockwell said in a statement demand for early samples of its K56 chips has been strong adding that the first modems using the technology should be in retail stores in March.

The company said it expects 135 of its customers to deploy the K56 chipsets by the end of the year. Rockwell's customers serve more than 70 percent of the worldwide market for client-side modems and 60 percent of the worldwide market for central-site modems.
"By mid-1997, our customers expect that they will have deployed several million K56 connections throughout the nation," said Dwight Decker, Rockwell Semiconductor Systems president.
Rockwell's K56 modem chipsets allow Internet users to connect to the Internet over conventional telephone lines at almost twice currently available speeds.
Modem maker U.S. Robotics Corp has developed a competing technology called "x2." To date Rockwell and U.S. Robotics have not worked out standards for the two technologies to be interoperable.
